necessary_context.applies_to: Theorem 7, Theorem 8 and the recorded OGD variant
necessary_context.content: H is a real Hilbert space with its Hilbert norm. F:H→R is differentiable, F*=inf F>−∞, and for every x,y, F(y)−F(x)=integral_0^1 <grad F(x+t(y−x)),y−x>dt. The stochastic oracle uses fresh iid samples z, has mean grad F(x), and variance at most sigma^2 at each query point. Adaptive-query use requires these properties conditionally at the actual query.
necessary_context.name: Standing setup and Definition 1

necessary_context.applies_to: Interpretation of Corollary 9 and the deferred explicit OGD corollary
necessary_context.content: Definition 5 defines ||grad F(x)||_delta as the infimum of |||S|^(-1)sum_{y in S}grad F(y)|| over nonempty finite subsets S of B(x,delta) whose uniform mean is x. Definition 4 states the corresponding finite-support stationarity notion, but its displayed gradient expectation uses z after introducing y. The algorithm naturally supplies a list of sampled points, possibly with repetitions; this record does not identify a finite multiset with a literal finite subset.
necessary_context.name: Definitions 4 and 5

necessary_context.content: For K blocks of T rounds, R_T(u^1,...,u^K)=sum_{k=1}^K sum_{n=(k−1)T+1}^{kT}<g_n,Delta_n−u^k>. The block comparators used by Theorem 8 depend on the realized true gradients of the whole block.
necessary_context.name: K-shifting regret
